historical_anchor: Postwar USAAF analysis judged Fourteenth Air Force interdiction costly and delaying but insufficient to stop the Hunan advance; Japanese movement exploited darkness, defended ports and rapid repair.
priority_targets: Yangtze-Xiang feeder shipping and rail yards
exposed truck columns and artillery parks
forward Japanese airfields and fuel dumps
tactical support of Chinese rearguards when target intelligence is fresh
airfield_policy: Do not leave large 14AF/CACW inventories to be captured at Changsha/Xiangtan. Forward servicing remains active while aircraft rotate south/west as the ground threat approaches; demolition packages are prepared before abandonment.
net_assessment: Interdiction materially slows bridge/road repair and increases Japanese fuel/vehicle costs, but does not close the Wuhan-Yueyang-Miluo logistics system. Allied air power preserves value by forcing dispersal and night movement rather than seeking an unsustainable decisive air battle.
